title: Vitamin D (25-hydroxy)

review.note: Drafted from the source below; not yet reviewed by a medical professional.

measures: A vitamin D test measures the level of vitamin D in the blood. Most tests measure a form called 25-hydroxyvitamin D, which is the most accurate way to see if the body has enough vitamin D for healthy bones, muscles, nerves, and the immune system.
context: The body makes vitamin D from sunlight on the skin, and gets it from a few foods and from supplements. Medicines, vitamins, and supplements can affect the result, so it helps to tell your provider about them.
aboveRange: Higher levels usually can be associated with getting too much vitamin D from supplements
belowRange: Lower levels may be associated with not getting enough vitamin D from diet or sunlight
May be associated with trouble absorbing vitamin D from food
May be associated with trouble changing vitamin D into a usable form, which can be linked to some kidney or liver conditions
May be associated with taking a medicine that affects vitamin D levels
nextStep: Discuss this result with your doctor.
